rows.answer: The supplied evidence does not identify the specific languages used in “Empirical Gaussian priors for cross-lingual transfer learning.” It only describes cross-lingual part-of-speech tagging using source language models and does not list the languages. Therefore, the evidence is insufficient to answer the question.

The paper uses the MNCut spectral clustering algorithm. The authors state that they apply an off-the-shelf clustering algorithm on top of the target-language vectors to group verbs into classes and, following prior work, employ MNCut spectral clustering [2]; the number of clusters is estimated using the self-tuning method [3].

rows.answer: The results were presented using precision, recall, and F$_1$ at the entity level, based on exact matches after extracting and deduplicating all tagged spans for each content element type [1]. These metrics were computed across all content elements in a micro-averaged manner and also broken down by type [2]. For the data-efficiency analysis, only F$_1$ scores were shown, although similar trends were observed for the other metrics [3].
